Layout stage v2: nearest hub spacing 8 cm

All 8 required master rows are present. Source, temporal and metadata flags remain visible; completion does not establish a scientific winner.

Updated user constraint: Circle may grow as large as needed to use 8 cm nearest-center spacing. Equal projected width is not a goal for this primary layout decision. The new eight-case manifest excludes two equal-box references from the required set because of that explicit user instruction, not a data-driven selection. The unchanged historical ten-case manifest and its old equal-box/nearest-spacing preview remain available; completed equal-box results remain in master and do not block this stage.

The flat Circle at 8 cm nearest hubs has projected box width 26.9337 cm, projected maximum disk span 28.5250 cm and maximum hub-center diameter 20.9050 cm. These are different geometric measures; a larger box does not imply every size measure is larger. Tables retain the actual flat/tilted size metrics.

The scope was frozen at 2026-11-02T03:02:21.403587+00:00, before Circle fine-grid outcomes were known as directed by root. Earlier Square and Circle medium data were available, so this is not blind whole-study preregistration. Later Circle optimization respects the updated maximum nearest-center spacing of 8 cm; older 8.659/10 cm exploratory cases remain in master, outside this updated limit. This standalone view does not edit master rankings.

This stage contains flat models and one fixed 10° inward-thrust probe (outer edges raised); narrow angle optimization comes later. It is not a master case filter: all 67 completed master rows remain in the master report, including other completed tests, controls and unqualified measured rows.

7.62 cm finite actuator disks, 12 mm forcing thickness, modeled total electrical budget 19.29230769 W. Native CPU Foundation14 GAMG serial/direct profile be7 and unchanged C29 forcing are required. Electrical/shaft powers are inferred through the assumed loss map, not measured motor or battery power. Blade phase, common RPM, synchronized blade passage, stock fuselage/guards and a calibrated motor map are unresolved.

Medium and fine grids remain separate. Circle may have a larger projected box. Within each layout, flat and tilted cases share exactly the same hub positions. This fixed tilt probe does not establish an optimized angle.

Fine-grid instantaneous velocity snapshots

Actual native ParaView slices at t = 1.2 s, z = −4 cm, viewed along +z, with identical camera, crop and 0–12 m/s scale. These are instantaneous CFD velocity fields, not time-averaged flow or geometry drawings. The force labels separately use the 0.8–1.2 s means. Actuator forcing does not resolve blades, phase or synchronization; upstream coarse initialization numerics differ across layouts. Native PNGs, geometry and source/copy/display hashes are delivered in flow_sources/ and flow_provenance.json.

Flat span/hull metrics are analytic. Tilted projected-ellipse hulls use converged angular sampling with conservative geometry bounds, recorded in the frozen manifest and CSV/JSON. These geometry-discretization bounds are not CFD uncertainty estimates.

Protocol and upstream initialization limitations

Target comparison checks hold rotor count, D/h, electrical budget/loss law, validation role, native numerical signature, mapped initialization regime, 0.6 s start/source time, and 0.8–1.2 s primary window. Frozen input hashes and completed master geometry/metadata are checked. Input failures and measured values remain visible instead of being removed.

Upstream coarse initialization is confounded across layout families. The Square mapped fields came from legacy coarse MPI2/direct-coarsest-off sources, while Circle sources used serial/direct-coarsest-on. These verified profile differences are retained below. Equal target methods and finite settling time do not eliminate the difference in initialization history; this report makes no isolated layout-effect claim. Unknown upstream evidence also cannot establish a match.

† denotes the existing absolute row late-window lift/input screen failing or unavailable. It is distinct from paired gain stability. The row screen uses the master tolerance (normally 0.25% mean-lift half drift), independently qualified primary/half windows and inferred-input agreement. Pair flags are copied from stored master diagnostics when present; otherwise the existing master pair helper uses cached master half-window metrics, without rerunning histories. Their provenance is listed in CSV/JSON. None is a confidence interval or proof of stationarity, mesh independence, physical gain or a global optimum.

The unchanged assumed loss map reserves 0.5 W electronics, 95% ESC efficiency, 0.10 W idle loss per motor, 60% motor conversion and 50% axial forcing fraction: Pshaft=0.60·[0.95·(Pe−0.5)−0.10N], Pair=0.50Pshaft, shared equally among rotors. The 19.29 W reference comes from nominal 4.18 Wh divided by advertised 13 min forward-flight endurance; it is not measured hover or maximum power, and reproducing 13 min by division is not validation. No efficiency was fitted to mass.

Root-reviewed interpretation

At 8 cm nearest rotor-center spacing, the square has slightly higher sampled mean vertical lift at both tested inclinations and both mesh levels. On the fine grid, flat square/circle values are 1.29526/1.29194 N; inward-10-degree values are 1.31068/1.30818 N. The square leads by about 0.26% flat and 0.19% tilted. These small differences do not establish an inherent layout advantage: relative differences change with refinement, and the upstream coarse initialization uses different execution/numerical settings. The fine-window ordering is consistent, but these are not independent statistical replicates.

Both layouts remain credible. Use the square as a provisional working reference because its sampled means are consistently higher; do not permanently eliminate the circle. The circle is allowed to grow to 8 cm neighbor spacing under the revised instruction. Its hub-circle diameter is 20.905 cm and flat propeller maximum span is 28.525 cm. Its 26.934 cm width/length differs from the square's 23.620 cm; the square has a larger 30.247 cm maximum span. Equal nearest spacing does not mean equal overall width, maximum span or hull area.

At these tested points, inward 10 degrees increases fine-grid mean lift by 1.1905% for the square and 1.2569% for the circle. Both fine pairs pass the finite late-window screens, but the gains decrease from medium to fine grids. This stage does not identify an optimal angle or establish grid-independent gain. The narrow medium-circle drift failure remains visible in the data rather than being discarded.

These are transient OpenFOAM actuator-volume results with 7.62 cm propeller-sized regions, a 19.2923 W total modeled electrical budget and documented assumed power losses. The model shares one interacting flow field, but does not resolve blades, synchronization phase, common-RPM fixed-pitch operation, airframe forces or measured motor performance. The figures therefore describe the stated model, not measured Tello lift or a global optimum. Rotor-count comparison and the wider angle/spacing stage follow this layout report.
